questions.q: If she ___ earlier, she will catch the bus.
questions.e: Use the present after “if” for a real future possibility.

questions.q: They have ___ their homework already.
questions.e: After “have”, use the past participle.

questions.q: You ___ wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle.
questions.e: Use “should” to give advice.

questions.q: We ___ at the station when the train arrived.
questions.e: Use “were waiting” for an action in progress in the past.

questions.q: He is taller ___ his brother.
questions.e: Use “than” after a comparative adjective.

questions.q: There isn't ___ sugar left in the jar.
questions.e: Use “much” with uncountable nouns like sugar.

questions.q: She has lived here ___ 2022.
questions.e: Use “since” with the starting point in time.

questions.q: I have known him ___ three years.
questions.e: Use “for” with a length of time.

questions.q: The match was ___ because of the rain.
questions.e: The passive uses “was” and a past participle.

questions.q: My sister enjoys ___ novels.
questions.e: After “enjoy”, use a verb ending in -ing.

questions.q: We ___ visit our grandparents next weekend.
questions.e: Use “be going to” for a planned future action.

questions.q: You don't have to ___ the whole book today.
questions.e: After “have to”, use the base verb.

questions.q: The parcel ___ yesterday afternoon.
questions.e: Use the simple past for a finished time yesterday.

questions.q: He asked me where I ___.
questions.e: In reported speech, “live” often moves back to “lived”.

questions.q: This exercise is ___ than the last one.
questions.e: Short adjectives usually take -er in a comparison.

questions.q: We should leave now, ___ we will miss the bus.
questions.e: “Or” introduces the bad result of not acting.

questions.q: I haven't seen Awa ___ Monday.
questions.e: Use “since” with a named starting day.

questions.q: The children were tired, ___ they finished the race.
questions.e: “But” joins contrasting ideas.

questions.q: There are ___ chairs for everyone.
questions.e: Use “enough” before a plural noun.

questions.q: He speaks English ___ than he did last year.
questions.e: Use the comparative form “better”.

questions.q: The room is too dark ___ read in.
questions.e: Use “too + adjective + to” for something not possible.

questions.q: If it rains, we ___ indoors.
questions.e: Use “will” in the result of a real future condition.

questions.q: She was cooking while I ___ the table.
questions.e: Use the simple past for the shorter action in the past.

questions.q: They have never ___ to Saint-Louis.
questions.e: After “have”, use the past participle “been”.
